Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

in short phrase

also to sum up, in a word, all in all, taken as a whole, on the whole, why say more?, need I say more?, make it brief, be brief, keep it short

classical

Cic. Att. 14.1.1: ad summam: nōn posse istaec sīc abīre (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 108, 408

ad summam

adverbial phrase

in short, in a word, on the whole

Other words

  • in summā — in a word, in fine

    also used · classical · Quint. 9.2.72 (Lewis & Short s.v. in); Traupman 108

  • in summam — taken as a whole, overall

    also used · classical · Quint. 4.2.90: quaedam partibus blandiuntur, sed in summam nōn cōnsentiunt (Lewis & Short); Traupman 108, 111, 407

    Of the whole set against its parts.

  • Quid plūra? — why say more? in short

    also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 2.3: hīc sacra, hīc genus, hīc majōrum multa vestīgia. quid plūra? (Lewis & Short s.v. multus); Traupman 111, 407

    Elliptical: “why (should I say) more?”; so also quid multa?.

  • breviter — briefly, in a word

    also used · classical · Traupman 147

    Properly “briefly, in few words”; ad summam is the colloquial “in short”.

Examples

  • In pauca cōnfer (cōnferte).

    Make it brief.Traupman 33

See also summarize, to make a long story short.
